discovery: Intermittency and multifractal structure of fully developed turbulence

nominees.name: Uriel Frisch
nominees.affiliation: Observatoire de la Côte d'Azur, CNRS, Nice, France

motivation: Turbulence is the oldest unsolved problem of classical physics: simple to state, very hard to understand. Kolmogorov's 1941 theory predicted self-similar scaling, but real flows are intermittent. Uriel Frisch led the theoretical move beyond Kolmogorov. With colleagues he developed the beta-model and the multifractal description of the energy cascade, and he built the modern statistical framework for anomalous scaling. Katepalli Sreenivasan carried out the decisive experiments. Measurements at very high Reynolds numbers in the laboratory and the atmosphere established that dissipation and velocity increments are multifractal, and they quantified anomalous exponents with unprecedented precision. Together their work turned intermittency from an anomaly into a quantitative science. The multifractal concept has since spread to finance, climate, cosmology and disordered systems. It is a deep conceptual advance that combines bold experiment with new mathematical ideas, revealing hidden order in apparent chaos.
